title: DR1 lays the review page out as six numbered sections with a named subsection above every card; the frontend uses three, and files several answers under a different section from DR1.

finding.frontend: The frontend shows three numbered sections — "1. About the consignment", "2. Movement", "3. Addresses" — plus a conditional "4. Documents". Section 1 carries three plain group headings, "Consignment details", "Commodity details" and "Species", and under them three cards: "Import details", "Additional animal details" (which holds Certified for, Includes unweaned animals, Reason for import and Purpose in the market together) and one card per species titled "Cow (0102) — Bos taurus" (which holds commodity code, common name, species, number of animals, number of packages and the animal identifier table together). Section 2 holds "Arrival details" — with the transit countries as a row inside it — and "Transport details". Section 3 holds "Roles and addresses" and "Contact address for this consignment". The section and group names are fixed strings in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:35-44, and the three sections are assembled in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/index.js:15-21.
finding.prototype: DR1 shows six numbered sections, each with a subsection heading above each card that names what the card answers — app/views/review-notification.html:40-176. They are: "1. About the consignment" ("Where is this consignment coming from?" → Import details; "What are you importing?" → Animal details; "Main reason for import" → Main reason for import); "2. Description of the goods" ("Commodity details" → a Commodity details card grouped by commodity; "Identification details" → one card per species carrying the animal table; "Additional details" → Certified for and Includes unweaned animals); "3. Transport and arrival" ("Arrival details"; an optional "Transit countries" card of its own; "Transport details"); "4. Documents" ("Upload documents" → Uploaded documents); "5. Consignment parties" ("Roles and addresses"); "6. Contact address" ("Contact address for this consignment"). So DR1 separates what the frontend fuses: reason for import gets its own card in section 1 rather than sharing one with the animal welfare answers; the commodity figures and the animal identifiers become two cards in section 2 rather than one; and transit countries become a card rather than a row.
finding.difference: Rebuild the section list to DR1's six, add the subsection heading above every card, and move four blocks of content: Reason for import and Purpose in the market out of the "Additional animal details" card into their own "Main reason for import" card in section 1; Certified for and Includes unweaned animals into an "Additional details" card in section 2; the animal identifier table out of the species card into an "Identification details" card in section 2, leaving the commodity figures behind in a "Commodity details" card; and the transit-countries row out of "Arrival details" into a card of its own. All of it is view-model and copy work in the check-answers feature — no answer is added or removed, only regrouped and relabelled — so it can land in one pass and its test is the rendered heading order. Land the page-heading change with it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the frontend review page rendering a section numbered 5 or 6, or any subsection heading phrased as a question such as "Where is this consignment coming from?".
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both screenshots; ran the falsifier — grep over fe-check-answers.html for a section numbered 5 or 6 and for "Where is this consignment"/"What are you importing" returns only SVG path data, so it does not fire. Walked the DR1 DOM heading by heading against the six sections and eleven cards the finding lists, and read copy.en.js:35-44 and view-model/index.js:15-20 on the frontend. Every regrouping the finding names is visible in the two pictures. CORRECT.
finding.correction: The claim stands and the six sections, their numbers, their subsection headings and all four content moves are confirmed in the captured DOM. One mis-citation, slot left alone: the DR1 range should be app/views/review-notification.html:41-179 — :40 is a blank line and section 6 closes at :179. One clarification, not a change: the Transit countries card is conditional in DR1 (review-notification.html:150-153 wraps it in an if) and is absent from the captured state, so the finding's word "optional" is right and there is no picture of that card on this corpus.

relatedTo.why: the Documents section is one of the six and its always-on behaviour is part of the same layout
